To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people with a high Conformism value are less likely to behave altruistically than are people who have a low Conformism value.
people low, but (not) high, in Confor-mism values are (more) motivated by self-transcendent values and (less) motivated by self-enhancement values.
people who consider conformity to be less important are more likely to behave in a self-transcendental manner and to experience regret for not doing so.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why some people behave more altruistically than others.
the role of values in the formation of anticipated regret and in the motivation of altruistic behavior.
the role of anticipated regret in motivating value-consistent behavior in social situations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relation between personal values and behavior depends on how strongly people adhere to social norms.
Conformism moderates the relations between values, anticipated regret, and behavior, and that Conformism is not a value itself. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2007 APA, all rights reserved)
Conformism moderates the relation between self-transcendent values and altruistic behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Conformism values can be seen as a moderating factor between values and behavior.
Conformism moderates the relations between values, anticipated regret, and behavior.
people who are low in Conformism are more likely than people who are high in Conformism, to behave according to their personal values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people are more likely to behave in ways that are congruent with their own values, when these values are consistent with social norms.
people who are low in Conformism are more likely to act in a manner that reflects their values.
Conformism values may moderate the relations between other value orientations and behavior.
